metadata.summary: Direct cardiac reprogramming relies on a combination of canonical cardiac transcription factors, typically consisting of Mef2c, Gata4, and Tbx5 (MGT). However, successful lineage conversion requires additional endogenous factors that coordinate the chromatin and transcriptional changes underlying fibroblast-to-cardiomyocyte conversion. Here, we identify Activating Transcription Factor 7 (Atf7) as a critical supporting factor that enables efficient direct cardiac reprogramming. These findings support a bifunctional regulatory role of Atf7 in promoting cardiomyocyte-specific gene activation while repressing fibroblast-associated transcriptional networks.

observations.text:
BackgroundKano State has one of the highest concentrations of zero-dose (ZD) children in Nigeria, challenging equitable immunization coverage. Digital engagement tools meant to strengthen timely data to address such gaps often underperform due to limited adaptability to user needs. Learning-by-doing (LxD), which brings together human-centered design and adaptive management, offers more context-responsive solutions.

Intervention and Implementation ApproachMCH-Track, a digital platform for tracking and referral for childhood vaccinations was used by 56 female community mobilizers in two local government areas (LGAs) out of the 44 LGAs in Kano State, Nigeria. We conducted a program case study from: 1) August 2024-April 2025 (initial implementation); and 2) adapted implementation (May 2025-November 2025), where LxD was incorporated to address emergent challenges. LxD included structured shadowing, monthly interviews with users, after-action reviews, and change log to track adaptations alongside routine services. Performance was monitored using four indicators: feedback actioned, response time-to-user feedback, ease-of-use score, and mobilizer performance in tracking ZD children.

FindingsAfter incorporating LxD, 17 issues were identified and led to 12 prioritized adaptations. All logged issues received responses, with median response time declining to approximately two weeks, while community mobilizers reported higher usability of the digital platform (e.g., mean ease-of-use score of 4.1 out of 5). Enhanced root-cause analysis enabled trend tracking and clearer escalation pathways for systemic issues like micro-stockouts at immunization points. Empathy tool records revealed mobilizer struggles with platform. This was immediately logged, prompting user experience redesign into a seamless, single-step process from registration-to-referral. During the LxD implementation period, an average of 33 ZD children per month were identified via MCH-Track, a substantial increase from the pre-LxD period (an average of 11 ZD children identified per month). Average referral-to-access rates also improved during the LxD period, rising from 44% of identified and referred ZD children accessing immunization services pre-LxD to 70% after incorporating LxD practices.

ConclusionEmbedding LxD within MCH-Track strengthened co-creation, streamlined workflows, and improved community mobilizer performance, demonstrating the value of adaptive management in reaching ZD children.

Teaser MessageIntegrating learning-by-doing approaches - mixture of human-centered design and adaptive management - into a digital community-engagement platform improved understanding of previously under-recognized vaccination barriers, implementing locally tailored adaptations, and strengthening frontline responsiveness to reach zero-dose children in Kano State, Nigeria.

observations.text: Ion channels remain notoriously recalcitrant drug targets despite their extensive pathophysiological significance. Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are proton-gated cation channels that cause neuronal death when excessively activated, such as during ischaemic stroke. This acidosis-driven injury pathway remains unchallenged by existing therapeutics. Here we generate two de novo designed hASIC1a-specific miniproteins by developing a platform that integrates computational miniprotein design, high-throughput automated patch clamp screening, biophysical and structural characterisation, and in vivo validation. We identify a subtype-selective hASIC1a inhibitor, Denasin1, which achieves near-complete inhibition with nanomolar potency. Denasin1 is disordered in solution but adopts the computationally predicted helix-turn-helix fold when bound to the extracellular acidic pocket of hASIC1a. Crucially, Denasin1 reduces infarct volume by > 50% in a murine model of ischaemic stroke. We thereby establish our de novo design platform as a route to develop potent and selective ion channel modulators.
observations.title: A deep learning-generated hASIC1a miniprotein inhibitor confers neuroprotection in stroke

metadata.summary: Atherosclerotic plaque rupture is a major cause of myocardial infarction and stroke. However, the precise drivers of plaque destabilisation remain elusive. We hypothesised that antigen-driven, autoimmune-like T cell responses are central to the destabilisation and rupture of atherosclerotic plaques. To dissect T cell responses specifically in unstable compared to stable plaques, we leveraged near-infrared autofluorescence (NIRAF) imaging-guided dissection of human carotid plaques and our tandem stenosis model in mice. We applied single-cell multi-omics to study T cell differentiation states and T cell receptor (TCR) repertoires. T cell responses in unstable versus stable atherosclerosis were distinct. Unstable human plaques contained highly expanded, autoimmune-like CD8+ T cells with markedly increased cytotoxic signatures, reduced exhaustion and distinct clonal repertoires compared to stable regions. Most plaque CD8+ T cells exhibited a pronounced tissue-resident transcriptional program. Autoimmune-like cytotoxic and tissue-resident CD8+ T cell responses were also evident in murine atherosclerosis, where restricting the activation of antigen-driven CD8+ T cells prevented plaque destabilisation.

observations.text: Fluorescent proteins have transformed biological imaging, yet their limited photostability and brightness restrict their applications. We used deep learning-based de novo protein design methods to design binders to three bright, stable and cell-permeable dyes spanning the imaging spectrum: JF657 (far red), JF596 (orange-red) and JF494 (green). We obtain highly specific dye-binding proteins with low nanomolar affinities for the intended target; a crystal structure of one binder confirms close resemblance to the design model. Simultaneous labeling of mammalian cells expressing three dye-specific binders at different subcellular compartments demonstrates the utility in multiplex imaging. We further expand the functionality of the binder by incorporating an active site that carries out nucleophilic aromatic substitution to form a covalent linkage with the dye, and develop split versions which reconstitute fluorescence at subcellular locations where both halves are present towards monitoring in-cell protein interactions and chemically induced dimerization. Our designed high affinity and specificity dye binders open up new opportunities for multiplexed biological imaging.
observations.title: Design of Orthogonal Far-Red, Orange and Green Fluorophore-binding Proteins for Multiplex Imaging

metadata.summary: Tumor heterogeneity arises from the sequential acquisition of somatic mutations and the selection of fitter clones, leading to distinct genotypes and phenotypes. Joint mapping of genome and transcriptome in the same tumor tissue can directly link clonoal relation to transcriptional state enabling a more in-depth understanding of intrinsic and extrinct tumor heterogeneity in the tissue context. Here, we introduce Spatial-GT-seq, a spatial multi-omic technology capable of genome-wide co-profiling of the genome and transcriptome at near single-cell resolution. We demonstrated in situ identification of tumor subclones in a mouse model of lung metastasis, with parallel transcriptomic profiles indicating that the gene expression profile of the same tumor clone is altered by the tumor microenvironment. Furthermore, analysis of primary and recurrent human pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors reveals both persistent and newly emerging tumor subclones, exhibiting transcriptional changes in both the original and recurrence sites. These findings highlight Spatial-GT-seq as a valuable platform for studying genotype-phenotype-microenvironment associations, providing new insights into cancer evolution and heterogeneity.

observations.text: The self-splicing group I intron ribozyme from Tetrahymena thermophillia (THr) is a prototypical example of how RNA overcomes its limited chemical repertoire to form complex, negatively charged junctions and catalyze chemical reactions. Despite over 30 years of biochemical and structural characterization, questions still remain regarding the requirements for THr catalysis that may inform structure based drug design against group I introns, as well as the use of THr as an RNA editing tool. Recent cryo-EM structures have provided an unprecedented window into the first and second steps of splicing, enabling detailed mechanistic investigation at the atomistic level. In this work, we leverage solvation theory, molecular dynamics, alchemical free energy simulations, and machine learning accelerated QM/MM to probe outstanding questions related to 1) the role of a possible third Mg2+ binding in the active site, 2) differences in catalytic requirements between Gexo cofactors and between the first and second steps of splicing, 3) the potential role of an acid or base, and 4) restrictions on the identity of the 5' exon splice site nucleotide, U(-1). We propose that a transient, cofactor dependent, interaction with a third metal participates in the first step, while a higher affinity interaction with this third ion is required in the second step. We also propose that the presence of a phosphate on the Gexo in the first step, and analogously the G{omega} in the second step, forms a metal ion binding site not present when guanosine is bound. Finally, we propose and computationally test design modifications of G22 (isofunctional substitutions of 2,6-diaminopurine that tune the pKa at the N1 position) that we predict will enable the accommodation of C(-1) in a crucial wobble-like pair at physiological pH. This design would provide a potential strategy for expanding the sequence space accessible to programmable trans-splicing ribozymes in RNA editing applications.
observations.title: A transient third metal ion shapes the catalytic cycle of a group I intron ribozyme

observations.text: Cardiac amyloidosis is caused by deposits of misfolded proteins in the heart and can lead to heart failure. Histological confirmation typically involves staining tissue sections with Congo red and examining them under polarized light for apple-green birefringence; however, achieving an interpretable, label-free, and observer-independent assessment remains challenging. Here we show that Pearson kurtosis of channel intensities within the amide I window provides an interpretable, fitting-free contrast for cardiac amyloid in unstained human cardiac tissue sections imaged by ultrabroadband multiplex coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (CARS). In two participants, high-kurtosis regions corresponded with Congo red-positive tissue in adjacent stained sections (descriptive spatial AUCs, 0.79 and 0.73). Across 15 fields from nine participants, including one of these two, kurtosis values did not overlap between severe-deposition and amyloid-negative tissue. Among the descriptors examined, kurtosis showed the largest standardized participant-level separation. Exploratory multivariate curve resolution yielded a deposit-associated component with aromatic-residue features shared with reagent transthyretin. Second harmonic generation (SHG), acquired simultaneously with CARS, showed a broadly inverse spatial pattern relative to kurtosis, providing complementary architectural contrast. These findings support a label-free approach to detecting cardiac amyloid deposits that combines broadband CARS-derived amide I kurtosis with SHG.

observations.text: Osteoporosis is a major global health concern, yet screening remains inaccessible in many economically challenged and low-resource settings due to the high cost and operational complexity the gold standard Dual-energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DXA) scan requires. This study presents a multimodal deep-learning approach for opportunistic osteoporosis screening using chest X-rays and clinical variables such as age and gender. A total of 406 samples were retrospectively collected from a national hospital, comprising annotated chest radiographs paired with their DXA results from patients 50 and above. Two convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, ResNet50 and EfficientNetb3, were deployed under three configurations: image-only, early fusion, and late fusion. Image preprocessing includes CLAHE+Gamma Correction, followed by resizing, local regions of interest (ROI) extraction, and augmentation. observations.text: Understanding how receptor-level modulation reorganizes large-scale brain circuits remains a central challenge in neuropharmacology. Here we introduce a multiscale mechanistic model with explicit core-matrix thalamocortical architecture to examine how propofol reorganizes brainwide activity from individual receptors to systems-level circuits. Crucially, the model did not involve machine learning or statistical fitting to pre-existing anesthesia data. We use the model to simulate the multi-scale effects of propofol, which range from modulation of individual synaptic conductances to widespread alterations of neural spiking, field potentials, and coherence. Without requiring any training on task-specific data, our simulation of sensory processing in a standard auditory oddball paradigm matches independent data from anesthetized and awake behaving macaques. The same simulation, unmodified, also reproduces changes to functional connectivity in anesthetized humans, exhibiting selective attenuation of matrix thalamocortical loops relative to core loops. Most importantly, the simulation identified a previously unknown biomarker of propofol concentration: elevated residual inter-stimulus cortical activity. This dose-dependent biomarker was subsequently confirmed in empirical macaque data, where it had previously gone unnoticed. This simulation-first discovery, arising from mechanistic circuit dynamics rather than statistical comparison of clinical populations, serves as an illustrative example of a broader generative framework that can translate receptor-level modulation into circuit-scale biomarkers with potential applications across predictive neuropharmacology.

metadata.summary: Background: Direct reprogramming of cardiac fibroblasts (CFs) into induced cardiomyocytes (iCMs) holds promise as a therapeutic strategy for heart regeneration. Post-myocardial infarction (MI), resident quiescent CFs (QCFs) activate and differentiate into myofibroblasts (MFs) in the infarcted region that drive pathological cardiac fibrosis. Converting these injury-activated MFs into iCMs could simultaneously alleviate fibrosis and replenish lost cardiomyocytes. However, whether the marked heterogeneity of CFs in the infarcted heart—and in particular the activation of QCFs into MFs—creates an intrinsic barrier that limits the reprogramming of these injury-activated MFs remains unknown. Methods: To define the molecular basis of this heterogeneity, we purified PDGFRα⁺ cardiac fibroblasts and used Postn lineage tracing to distinguish injury-activated MFs from quiescent CFs, enabling matched comparison of their reprogramming competence and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) profiling of post-MI CF subpopulations. A targeted in vitro shRNA screen was conducted against 9 MF-enriched TFs as candidate molecular barriers for cardiac reprogramming. The lead candidate was validated in mouse MFs, QCFs, human iPSC-derived MFs, primary human cardiac fibroblasts, and in vivo using dual-recombinase-mediated lineage tracing. Mechanistic insights were gained through integrated bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq and Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation (CUT&Tag), together with functional assays including DNA-binding–deficient and domain-swap MEOX1 mutants. Results: We identified the upregulated transcription factor MEOX1—a known fibrosis determinant downstream of the key post-MI cytokines TGF-β1 and IL-1β—as the principal molecular barrier responsible for the profound reprogramming resistance of MFs. MEOX1 knockdown markedly enhanced reprogramming efficiency in both mouse and human MFs and enabled GATA4-free reprogramming combinations. This inhibition depended on MEOX1’s transcriptional activation activity, as disrupting its DNA-binding domain or fusing it to a repressor domain rescued reprogramming. Integrated scRNA-seq and CUT&Tag analyses revealed that MEOX1 binds and stabilizes a fibrotic, MF-defining transcriptional program that antagonizes the cardiogenic program, while also modulating the inflammatory response; its knockdown disrupted this fibrotic network to favor iCM fate acquisition. Using stringent dual-recombinase lineage tracing, we demonstrated that MEOX1 knockdown enables highly efficient in vivo MF-to-iCM conversion, leading to significant reductions in cardiac fibrosis and substantial improvement in cardiac function after MI. Conclusions: Our study identifies the pathological upregulation of MEOX1 as a key mechanism underlying the reprogramming resistance of post-MI MFs, in both mouse and human. Overcoming this barrier achieves unprecedented, lineage-confirmed in vivo reprogramming efficiency, thereby addressing a significant obstacle for the clinical translation of in situ reprogramming therapies. Data included in this Series comprise the original bulk RNA-seq datasets of MGTM-reprogrammed mouse cardiac fibroblasts with control or Meox1 knockdown and with control vector/GFP or MEOX1 overexpression; RNA-seq datasets from human iPSCs, iPSC-derived cardiac fibroblasts, and iPSC-derived myofibroblasts; scRNA-seq datasets from MGTM-induced iCM cultures and normal or day-3 post-MI mouse hearts; MEOX1 CUT&Tag data; and the newly added three-biological-replicate bulk RNA-seq dataset comparing MGTM + shCtrl with MGTM + shMeox1 used for the revised manuscript.

GKT136901 attenuated structural remodeling, diastolic dysfunction indices, elevated filling pressures, and cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, but did not improve endurance. observations.text: The emergence of treatment resistant mutants is one of the primary contributors to therapy failure in cancer. Evolution-based adaptive therapies aim to exploit the competition between sensitive and resistant cells to prolong therapeutic control. However, in the densely packed tissues of solid tumors, competition is not only determined by cell-intrinsic factors but also a result of local physical interactions between neighboring cells. The successful development of physics-informed adaptive therapies therefore hinges upon the bottom-up integration of tissue mechanics and experimentally grounded models of tumor evolution. Here, we show how population-level treatment response emerges from mechanical interactions between individual cells. Combining genetically tailored therapy-mimicry experiments in spatially structured 2D melanoma colonies with mechanistic, particle-based tissue simulations as digital twins in a real-to-sim-to-real framework, we reveal how treatment-induced changes in mechanical crowding shape a cascade of resistance expansion, spatial competitive escape, and consequent therapy failure. We then link these underlying physical mechanisms to population-level observables in an abstracted mathematical model for reinforcement-learning-based therapy optimization and a distilled treatment-decision-heuristic, which we test experimentally. Together, our results identify mechanical crowding and escape as governing principles of resistance-mediated therapy failure in solid tumours and provide a basis for mechanistically informed, evolution-based treatment strategies.

Quantifying how extracurricular physical activity buffers this pathway remains difficult because daily movement durations inhabit a closed 24-hour simplex and both exposures share psychosocial confounding. Standard moderated regression and Euclidean dose-response estimators treat exercise volume as a free scalar, ignoring whether added activity displaces sedentary screen time or sleep. We formulate PhyBuff-Net, a compositional counterfactual dose-response network coupled with constrained isotemporal prescription optimization (CIPO), evaluated on a multi-school cohort of N=3,600 adolescents across junior high (n=1,600) and senior high (n=2,000) grades. On the held-out test split (N_test=720, five seeds) and five-split outer cross-validation under shared-donor evaluation, PhyBuff-Net achieves counterfactual surface determinations of 0.9566± 0.0105 and 0.9421± 0.0103 versus 0.9244± 0.0057 for stratified interaction networks and 0.8930± 0.0162 for contrastive balancing representation learning, lowers policy regret from 2.4729 to 1.8932, and eliminates circadian feasibility violations (0.00%). abstract Counterfactual dose-response estimation, Compositional data analysis, Isotemporal substitution, Smartphone addiction, Adolescent anxiety, Constrained prescription optimization Introductionsec:intro Adolescent smartphone overdependence and internalizing anxiety symptoms reinforce one another through disrupted nocturnal circadian regulation, elevated academic distress, and progressive social withdrawal kwon2013sassv,cao2023anxiety,zhang2025comorbidity. Across secondary school populations, elevated scores on the Smartphone Addiction Scale-Short Version (SAS-SV) consistently track higher scores on the 21-item Depression Anxiety Stress Scales (DASS-21) anxiety subscale. In a multi-grade senior high school cohort facing intensive examination schedules, 50.72% of students met the SAS-SV smartphone addiction criterion ren2022movement,lovibond1995dass,hua2025associations. Extracurricular physical activity (EPA) acts as a modifiable behavioral buffer that attenuates both addictive smartphone engagement and downstream anxious arousal; it is typically indexed on the Physical Activity Rating Scale (PARS, 3-item version PARS-3) or via 24-hour accelerometry huang2026temporal,peng2025abuse,qin2025smartphone. Estimating an individualized dose-response buffering curve from observational school cohorts nevertheless confronts a structural physical constraint aitchison1982simplex,chastin2015coda,dumuid2019isotemporal. Every adolescent's day sums strictly to 1,440 min across sleep (SLP), sedentary behavior (SB), light physical activity (LPA), and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA). Because 24-hour movement behaviors reside on a closed simplex, increasing extracurricular exercise by 30-60 min/day must draw an equal duration from at least one remaining behavioral compartment egozcue2003ilr,ren2022movement,byun2024screen. Reallocating time from recreational screen-based sedentary behavior into MVPA produces pronounced reductions in somatic and cognitive anxiety zhou2024replacing,hua2025associations. Drawing that same exercise duration from nocturnal sleep, among already sleep-restricted senior high school students, impairs sleep quality and exacerbates anxious distress qin2025smartphone,xiao2024relationship. Classical parametric moderated mediation models collapse this compositional substitution structure into a single linear product term. The standard instance is ordinary least squares (OLS) regression with bilinear interaction terms (PROCESS-OLS) hayes2018process,cao2023anxiety,peng2025abuse, which cannot capture threshold saturation or donor-specific sign reversals. Conversely, linear Compositional Data Analysis (CoDA) isotemporal substitution models respect closure on the Aitchison simplex chastin2015coda,dumuid2019isotemporal but assume homogeneous log-ratio slopes across the entire population, overlooking nonlinear interaction dynamics across mild, moderate, and severe smartphone addiction strata. Recent causal machine learning and continuous dose-response architectures relax parametric functional assumptions for continuous interventions shalit2017estimating,schwab2020drnet,feuerriegel2024causal. They include varying-coefficient neural networks (VCNet) nie2021vcnet, gradient interpolation and kernel smoothing (GIKS) nagalapatti2024giks, and contrastive balancing representation learning (CBRL) zhu2024cbrl. Despite their flexibility on univariate exposures, applying Euclidean dose-response estimators directly to adolescent physical activity and smartphone addiction reveals three methodological failure modes. First, Euclidean networks treat the target EPA dose D_EPA as a free scalar independent of the 24-hour movement vector t_i S^4_1440, ignoring donor-compartment heterogeneity and generating counterfactual allocations whose proportional sleep draws breach physiological sleep floors. Second, smartphone addiction A_i and physical activity dose D_EPA,i are jointly confounded by school adjustment, academic pressure, and family socioeconomic standing kim2022kyrbs,cao2023anxiety,zhou2025pretraining. Single-exposure balancing penalties leave the bivariate exposure distribution P(A, D_EPA x, t) coupled in off-diagonal regions where severe smartphone addiction coincides with high physical activity volume. Third, standard neural estimators issue unguarded point prescriptions without verifying whether a candidate exercise increment is supported by local observational density or executable within an adolescent's mandatory school schedule schweisthal2024reliable. We address these challenges in PhyBuff-Net, a compositional counterfactual dose-response network coupled with Constrained Isotemporal Prescription Optimization (CIPO) across four architectural components (C1-C4). A counterfactual dose must enter the model as a valid 24-hour composition rather than as a free scalar. In component one (C1), an Isometric Compositional Time-Reallocation Encoder (ICTE) maps each movement vector into orthonormal Helmert isometric log-ratio (ilr) coordinates and carries the donor choice through an explicit simplex reallocation. Deconfounding one margin of the exposure pair leaves the other biased, because (A, D_EPA) is selected jointly. In component two (C2), a Double-Continuous Contrastive Kernel Balancing Representation (DC-KBR) learner extends Kernel Balancing Representation (KBR) by penalizing residual dependence between the latent state and both exposures at once. It combines a conditional Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC) and quantile-stratified InfoNCE contrastive regularization with stabilized Gaussian-kernel density-ratio balancing weights. In component three (C3), the response surface is estimated through a Varying-Coefficient Orthogonal Buffering Spline (VC-OBS) head built on degree-M Bernstein polynomials with second-order knot smoothness. Unlike an unconstrained neural readout, VC-OBS returns zero-anchored closed-form buffering curves and analytical donor utility gradients. In component four (C4), prescriptions are optimized by the CIPO module over the learned surface. We evaluate the complete framework on a multi-school cohort of N = 3,600 de-identified adolescents spanning grades 7-12 with 12-week wave-2 longitudinal follow-up. Related Worksec:related Adolescent smartphone addiction, anxiety, and physical activity moderationsec:rel_domain Psychometric and epidemiological investigations establish a robust positive association between adolescent smartphone addiction and anxiety severity kwon2013sassv,lovibond1995dass,kim2022kyrbs. In junior high school cohorts, Cao et al. cao2023anxiety demonstrated that smartphone addiction measured via SAS-SV correlates positively with DASS-21 anxiety (r = 0.392) and negatively with school adjustment (r = -0.596). Physical activity measured on PARS-3 moderates and buffers the pathway from internalizing distress to problematic phone use. In a multi-grade senior high school investigation (N = 1,323), Ren et al. ren2022movement reported a 50.72% SAS-SV addiction rate. Within that cohort SAS-SV scores rise monotonically across no-anxiety (30.13 ± 9.03), mild (35.37 ± 8.52), moderate (41.70 ± 10.66), and severe (43.90 ± 13.70) anxiety strata. More recent cross-sectional and longitudinal studies confirm that extracurricular physical exercise mitigates internet and smartphone addiction comorbidity with anxiety peng2025abuse,zhang2025comorbidity,qin2025smartphone,xiao2024relationship. These empirical studies, however, rely on linear regression or Hayes PROCESS macro models hayes2018process that treat physical activity as a categorical moderator or a linear interaction term. Such models cannot estimate minimum effective exercise doses individually across a continuous addiction spectrum. Compositional data analysis on the 24-hour movement simplexsec:rel_coda Daily time-use epidemiology recognizes that sleep, sedentary behavior, light activity, and moderate-to-vigorous activity form a strictly closed composition summing to 1,440 min/day aitchison1982simplex,chastin2015coda. Egozcue et al. egozcue2003ilr introduced the isometric log-ratio (ilr) transformation, which maps simplex vectors onto unconstrained Euclidean coordinates under the Aitchison geometry. Dumuid et al. dumuid2019isotemporal formalized compositional isotemporal substitution, which quantifies health changes when fixed durations (e.g., 15-30 min/day) are reallocated from one movement behavior to another. Applied to student and adolescent health, compositional and isotemporal analyses show that replacing sedentary behavior with MVPA is associated with lower smartphone addiction (ilr_1 = -0.453 in adolescent CoDA ren2022movement) and reduced anxiety symptoms zhou2024replacing,hua2025associations. Insufficient sleep duration and sleep disorders run the other way and exacerbate anxious distress qin2025smartphone,xiao2024relationship. Parallel adolescent isotemporal substitution models likewise quantify screen-time reallocation trade-offs across somatic health markers byun2024screen. Nevertheless, existing compositional substitution methods remain parametric linear models without deconfounded representation learning, counterfactual surface estimation, or individualized donor-allocation optimization. Continuous dose-response and counterfactual representation learningsec:rel_causal Counterfactual representation learning originally addressed binary treatments by minimizing distributional divergence between treated and control covariates shalit2017estimating,wager2018causalforest,chernozhukov2018dml. Cross-fitted Double Machine Learning (DML) similarly orthogonalizes nuisance treatment and outcome regressions chernozhukov2018dml,wager2018causalforest. To handle continuous interventions, DRNet schwab2020drnet discretized dosage into strata, SciGAN bica2020scigan employed adversarial networks, and VCNet nie2021vcnet parameterized the outcome head as a varying-coefficient B-spline of the continuous dose. Subsequent advances introduced normalizing flows and missing-treatment estimators for interventional distributions melnychuk2023normalizing,kuzmanovic2023estimating, consensus-enabled robust counterfactual regression (CE-RCFR) wang2024cercfr, two-stage pretraining-finetuning under confounding zhou2025pretraining, and causal mediation frameworks farbmacher2022mediation,feuerriegel2024causal. Three lines bear most directly on our work. Adaptive spline plug-in estimators target nonparametric causal dose-response curves shi2026hal, and GIKS nagalapatti2024giks leverages gradient interpolation and kernel smoothing to regularize counterfactual derivatives in sparse dosage regions. Continuous-treatment representation learners instead decouple selection bias, through adversarial balancing kazemi2024counterfactual, Hilbert-Schmidt kernel independence gretton2005hsic, or contrastive balancing (CBRL) zhu2024cbrl. Yet none of these architectures respects compositional closure on a 24-hour time simplex or decouples joint selection bias across two interacting continuous exposures under physiological feasibility constraints schweisthal2024reliable. Positivity-constrained off-policy prescription and donor optimizationsec:rel_agent Reliable individualized treatment prescription from observational cohorts requires constraining candidate interventions to regions with sufficient overlap (positivity) and domain-specific physiological feasibility schweisthal2024reliable,feuerriegel2024causal,chernozhukov2018dml. Unconstrained neural predictors emit single-pass point optima that can extrapolate into low-density dosage tails or violate circadian and schedule invariants on the 24-hour time-use simplex dumuid2019isotemporal. Positivity-constrained off-policy optimization instead pairs functional outcome estimation with explicit polytope projection over feasible donor allocations, mirror-ascent optimization on the probability simplex, and local effective-sample-size shrinkage in sparse regions schweisthal2024reliable. In compositional dose-response estimation, coupling constrained isotemporal prescription optimization (CIPO) directly with a learned varying-coefficient surface ensures that every candidate EPA recommendation satisfies circadian sleep floors, mandatory study schedules, and local observational support before prescription selection. Estimating how extracurricular physical activity buffers the pathway from adolescent smartphone addiction to anxiety requires reconciling continuous causal representation learning with the compositional geometry of the 24-hour day. Across our multi-school cohort of N = 3,600 adolescents spanning junior and senior high school grades, standard moderated regressions and donor-agnostic neural estimators systematically misestimate the counterfactual response surface whenever exercise volume is treated as an unconstrained Euclidean scalar. Potential anxiety outcomes depend on a three-way interaction among baseline smartphone addiction severity (A_i), continuous exercise dose (D_EPA,i), and the donor movement compartment (w_i). Under screen-time substitution, adolescents in moderate and severe SAS-SV strata exhibit counterfactual anxiety reductions of 3.33-4.12 DASS-21 points across d [40, 80] zhou2024replacing. Conversely, when high exercise volumes are drawn from nocturnal sleep among sleep-restricted students without circadian boundary projection, sleep depletion erodes the psychological benefit once post-reallocation sleep drops below 420 min/day ren2022movement,hua2025associations,xiao2024relationship. Each architectural module addresses a distinct source of estimation or prescription bias (Tables tab:ablation-tab:misspec). The ICTE module (C1) embeds the 24-hour simplex S^4_1440 directly into orthonormal ilr coordinates and couples every counterfactual dose query to the donor reallocation operator T_simplex. Without C1, unprojected Euclidean log-duration regressions incur 2.000 min/day simplex closure drift (92.92% FVR and 3.1728 policy regret in w/o C1, degrading R^2_CF by -0.0737). DC-KBR (C2) extends continuous treatment balancing from univariate propensity matching nie2021vcnet,zhu2024cbrl to bivariate kernel, contrastive, and stabilized density-ratio balancing over (A_i, D_EPA,i), lowering off-diagonal severe-addiction RMSE from 2.9449 (w/o C2) and 4.8127 (CBRL) to 2.7378 (Table tab:failure). The VC-OBS Bernstein head (C3) keeps the estimated surface zero-anchored and smooth via second-order knot regularization, avoiding the -0.1504 R^2_CF degradation of an unconstrained MLP head. Finally, CIPO (C4) acts on the learned surface at prescription time, cutting policy regret from 3.2848 (w/o C4, 10.14% FVR) to 1.8932 (0.00% FVR) through C4b mirror-ascent donor optimization (Δ R^2_CF = +0.0512 over w/o C4b), C4a circadian boundary projection (eliminating the 8.22% violations of w/o C4a), and C4c local-ESS support regularization. Several methodological and empirical limitations bound the scope of these findings. First, although multi-wave longitudinal follow-up across baseline and 12-week wave-2 assessments anchors the reference dose-response lookup grids and supports out-of-wave validation (RMSE_fact = 1.8656), observational school cohorts remain subject to unmeasured confounding from genetic, familial, or classroom-level shocks; randomized isotemporal substitution trials are needed before translating estimated dose thresholds into clinical guidelines. Second, our compositional encoder partitions the 24-hour day into four aggregate compartments (SLP, SB, LPA, MVPA). Disaggregating sedentary behavior into recreational smartphone screen time versus mandatory classroom and homework seated time via objective mobile-sensing logs would further sharpen the donor-allocation optimizer (C4b). Third, extending CIPO to multi-week ecological momentary assessment wrist-actigraphy cohorts will be essential for prospective validation of dynamic, day-by-day exercise reallocation policies wang2024cercfr,zhou2025pretraining. Conclusionsec:conclusion PhyBuff-Net unifies isometric log-ratio compositional encoding, double-continuous contrastive kernel balancing, varying-coefficient orthogonal Bernstein splines, and constrained isotemporal prescription optimization into a coherent framework for compositional counterfactual dose-response learning. Evaluated across a multi-school adolescent cohort (N = 3,600; held-out N_test = 720 across five seeds), five-split outer cross-validation, and 12-week wave-2 longitudinal follow-up under shared-donor scoring, PhyBuff-Net achieves a counterfactual surface R^2_CF of 0.9566 ± 0.0105 on the canonical test split and 0.9421 ± 0.0103 across outer cross-validation. It reduces surface MISE to 1.6701 ± 0.2034, buffering PEHE_buf to 1.9369 ± 0.2670, and counterfactual policy regret to 1.8932 ± 0.4178 while maintaining a 0.00% circadian feasibility violation rate. Respecting 24-hour compositional closure and circadian sleep boundaries is therefore essential for reliable counterfactual dose-response estimation and safe behavioral prescription optimization. The data support investigation of transcriptional changes associated with oxidative stress, inflammation, and cell-death-related pathways.

ObjectiveVenous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of preventable inpatient mortality, while the real-world performance of mandated risk assessment and the potential for automating using electronic health record (EHR) data remain unclear. We evaluated completion, concordance with structured EHR data, clinical validity, and feasibility of EHR-supported VTE risk assessment assisted by machine learning.

Materials and MethodsWe analysed 577,904 admissions and 726,896 VTE assessment forms across five NHS hospitals between 2015 and 2025. Concordance and clinical validity were evaluated in 87,118 completed assessments from 2023 to 2024. Machine learning models compared clinician-recorded and EHR-derived risk factors in 74,372 encounters with an assessment completed within 14 hours of admission.

ResultsOverall completion was 96.7%, and timely completion improved from 47.4% in 2015 to 90.5% in 2024. Agreement between forms and EHR data was good for common risk factors (e.g. age [≥] 60 years: precision 0.95, recall 0.77), but low-prevalence variables were often under-documented in the forms (e.g. critical care admission: precision 0.20, recall 0.14). Despite these discrepancies, form-derived thrombosis risk was associated with increased VTE incidence (adjusted OR 3.31, 95% CI 2.81-3.90). Models using EHR-derived factors available within 14 hours achieved an AUROC of 0.709, compared with 0.704 for clinician-recorded variables.

DiscussionMuch of the information the risk assessment requires already exists in structured EHR data, and EHR-derived variables contained discriminative information comparable to that in clinician-recorded factors.

ConclusionRoutinely collected EHR data could support real-time pre-population of structured VTE assessments, thereby reducing documentation burden while preserving clinical validity.
observations.title: Machine Learning-Supported Efficient VTE Risk Assessment using Routinely Collected Electronic Health Record Data

metadata.summary: Background: Hypothermic oxygenated perfusion (HOPE) may extend donor heart preservation beyond conventional storage durations. We evaluated early graft function and myocardial cellular and metabolic integrity following porcine heart transplantation after 20 hours of HOPE.  Methods: Ten donor hearts underwent various preservation conditions: static cold storage (SCS) for 4 hours (n=2), HOPE for 4 hours (n=3), and HOPE for 20 hours (n=5), followed by heart transplantation (HT) in recipient pigs. Following implant and reperfusion, graft function was assessed over 3 hours by serial echocardiography, invasive hemodynamics, optical flow analysis, and vasoactive support scoring; myocardial tissue was analyzed by histopathology, flow cytometry, mitochondrial respirometry, transcriptomics, and proteomics.  Results: Ejection fraction, right atrial pressure and systolic blood pressure did not differ significantly between groups, and no graft met criteria for primary graft dysfunction. LV contractility was within normal range with comparable vasoactive support among all groups. Preservation-associated weight gain was greatest after HOPE 20h, and histopathology showed comparable findings with edema present in all cohorts, without fibrosis, thrombosis, or necrosis. Cardiomyocyte viability was preserved across all groups (HOPE 20h, 86%, HOPE 4h, 81%, and SCS 4h, 77%). Maximal oxygen consumption rate was elevated in HOPE 20h versus HOPE 4h and SCS 4h (p<0.01), while basal and non-mitochondrial respiration were similar. Transcriptomics and proteomics revealed minimal differences in gene and pathway expression among groups.   Conclusions: HOPE preserves donor heart viability, mitochondrial integrity, and ventricular function after 20 hours of ischemia in a porcine model, without evidence of primary graft dysfunction, supporting extended preservation for heart transplantation. Edema, recovery of function, and metabolic responses warrant further investigation with longer-term monitoring.

observations.title: Twenty-Hour Hypothermic Oxygenated Perfusion Preserves Myocardial Viability and Bioenergetics with No Primary Graft Dysfunction After Porcine Heart Transplantation
